modern audiences tend to tune out overly scripted videos. employee-generated content captures the real, transparent workplace moments that build genuine trust. you don't need a film degree or expensive gear—simple adjustments to your phone settings, lighting, and framing are all it takes to make your work shine. takeaway: your everyday work perspective is a strategic brand asset. external audiences and candidates are 3x more likely to trust real workplace moments over traditional advertising. more trustable 3x posts shared directly by employees generate up to 8x more engagement than official corporate channels. higher engagement 8x why your perspective matters

group photos of celebrations showcase workplace culture, human connection, and energy that audiences genuinely enjoy. tip: get consent before making and sharing content! viewers quickly scroll past most content featuring inanimate objects without human interaction. tip: feature colleagues discussing or presenting instead. candid behind-the-scenes team interactions showcase a positive work culture which increases audience trust. tip: keep clips short (10–15 secs) for the best engagement! if you've ever paused and wondered, 'is this actually worth sharing?', you're already halfway to spotting a great story. click on each card below to find out if you should share the depicted workplace moment. what makes a moment publishable? touch click on the thumbnail for more information. touch click on the thumbnail for more information. touch click on the thumbnail for more information.
‘people do not buy goods and services. they buy relations, stories, and magic.’ seth godin, 2005

photo, video, or both? here are some of the things to consider before choosing a format: photos are great for static milestones, clear text or graphics, individual spotlights, and awards where no motion is needed. videos are great for dynamic action, step-by-step physical demos, and moments where speech, sound, or laughter drive the story. photos & videos are great for documenting multi-faceted events—a photo captures the room, while a short video brings the energy to life! ready to test your new knowledge? try the activity on the next slide.
